title: Make the current user a dependency with OAuth2PasswordBearer
summary: Replace the hand-written token check in every endpoint with get_current_user, send WWW-Authenticate with the 401, clean up a leaking dependency_overrides with a fixture, and answer 403 for inactive users.

turns.user: every new endpoint i copy paste this token check. also hitting it without the header gives 422 not 401 which is weird

assistant.body: Let's take it step by step. Header() has no default, so a missing Authorization header is a missing required parameter to FastAPI, hence the 422. Making OAuth2PasswordBearer a dependency hands it the job of pulling out the Bearer token, and it answers 401 when the header is absent. get_current_user in auth.py checks the token and returns the user, and Annotated wraps that into a CurrentUser type. The 401 carries WWW-Authenticate: Bearer, the header HTTP requires on every 401. tokenUrl is where Swagger UI goes to fetch a token.

from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, status
from fastapi.security import OAuth2PasswordBearer

oauth2_scheme = OAuth2PasswordBearer(tokenUrl="token")


def get_current_user(token: Annotated[str, Depends(oauth2_scheme)]) -> User:
    user_id = decode_token(token)
    if user_id is None or user_id not in USERS:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
            detail="invalid token",
            headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"},
        )
    return USERS[user_id]


CurrentUser = Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)]

assistant.body: Great question! Put a function in app.dependency_overrides under get_current_user, and FastAPI calls it instead of the real dependency. A lambda returning a fake user logs the test in without any JWT.

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from app.auth import User, get_current_user
from app.main import app

app.dependency_overrides[get_current_user] = lambda: User(id=1, name="mpyw")

client = TestClient(app)


def test_read_me():
    response = client.get("/me")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json()["name"] == "mpyw"

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous test changed dependency_overrides at import time. It is one dict on the app, so an override set there stays until the pytest process exits and leaks into every other test file. The override has to go in per test and come out afterwards. A fixture clears it after its yield, and only the tests that want a logged in user ask for that fixture.

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from app.auth import User, get_current_user
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)


@pytest.fixture
def logged_in():
    app.dependency_overrides[get_current_user] = lambda: User(id=1, name="mpyw")
    yield
    app.dependency_overrides.clear()


def test_read_me(logged_in):
    response = client.get("/me")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json()["name"] == "mpyw"


def test_read_me_without_token():
    response = client.get("/me")
    assert response.status_code == 401
    assert response.headers["WWW-Authenticate"] == "Bearer"

turns.user: oh and users who left, is_active False. if their token hasn't expired they still get in. make that a 403

assistant.body: Sure. The check goes right before the return in get_current_user. The sed captures the leading spaces and reuses them with \1, so the two new lines sit at the same depth. Note: a test that overrides get_current_user skips this check along with everything else in it.
sed -i '' 's/^\( *\)return USERS\[user_id\]$/\1if not USERS[user_id].is_active:\n\1    raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="inactive user")\n&/' app/auth.py
